narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A temperature high of 29°C (84°F) is expected today with isolated evening showers and thunderstorms from 21:00 bringing 2.1 mm (0.08 in) of rain. Sky conditions will show early Overcast, turning to midday Partly cloudy and evening Mostly cloudy. Thunder possible, peaking tomorrow afternoon. Winds will be northerly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with gusts up to 37 km/h (20 kt). Peak UV index is 9.1 today. Air quality sits at AQI 82 (model estimate). The overnight low will be 19°C (66°F). As of 08:40, reports through 08:00: no rain; thunder; high so far 22°C (72°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 9 km/h (5 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Thursday will be mostly cloudy with 4 of 4 models wet and thunder likely. Friday will be partly cloudy with 4 of 4 models wet and thunder likely. Saturday has a 100% rain call, 4 of 4 models wet, partly cloudy skies, and thunder likely. Sunday will be mostly cloudy with 4 of 4 models wet and thunder likely. Monday will be mostly cloudy with 4 of 4 models wet and thunder likely. Tuesday will be partly cloudy with 3 of 3 models wet and thunder likely. Wednesday has a 100% rain call, 2 of 2 models wet, mostly cloudy skies, and thunder possible. Highs remain 28–30°C (82–86°F) across the period.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values ahead suggest thunderstorm potential across models: GFS at 1350 J/kg, ECMWF at 2240 J/kg, ICON at 1600 J/kg, UKMO at 2670 J/kg, and Best Match at 1860 J/kg. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) has issued no official severe weather warnings.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winds on Winam Gulf are forecast overnight at 5 km/h (2 kt) gusting 6 km/h (3 kt), then southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt), then into the evening at 10 km/h (5 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt); peak gust 26 km/h (14 kt). Sudden gusts well above the forecast wind are a hazard near any potential thunderstorm.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) — a 5 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1013.1 and 1015.3 hPa; near-steady over three days (+0.4 hPa). The pressure trend is +0.8 hPa, with lowest pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet, while GFS holds the best rain record at 93%. Today's call of 29°C (84°F) high, 19°C (66°F) low, and 2.1 mm (0.08 in) rain agrees with the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD)'s forecast of 29°C (84°F) high and 19°C (66°F) low. Across models today, daytime highs range from 28°C (82°F) in ECMWF to 29.5°C (85.1°F) in UKMO, and peak gusts span 18 km/h (10 kt) in GFS to 35.3 km/h (19 kt) in Best Match. GFS systematically under-forecasts peak wind and does not see this location's thunderstorms coming, placing it on the wrong side of its wind record. At Day+3, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) the weakest. Stored forecast data spans 94 days with 67 checks for the least-covered model at Day+0, providing a settled picture, though Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) has fewer checks than other models.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Wednesday. Sunday and Monday: all four models wet, highs around 29°C (85°F). Tuesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 29°C (84°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. ICON is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 29°C (84°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 93% of the time over 87 checks.
